items.title: Turn the recovered compact HUD into a capability-complete responsive pressure aperture instead of silently bypassing the desktop HUD and dropping live run state.
items.why: HUD.jsx selects MobileHUD for desktop whenever hud?.useCompactDesktop is not exactly false, but hudFlags() never emits that property. The compact branch therefore wins for every normal density and is not passed objective/contract, grenade/dash readiness, reduced-effects state, missions, combo, or several feedback capabilities. This violates the master plan's desktop/mobile parity contract even though the component renders cleanly.
items.recipe: Define an explicit responsive-HUD contract and a pure urgency-ranked run-intel model. Preserve the clean top/bottom frame, add literal ability readiness and current objective/contract signals, keep secondary rivalry/integrity/drill/performance evidence behind one accessible expandable rail, make tactical density retain its richer desktop presentation, and add behavioral tests proving capability parity at mobile, compact desktop, and tactical desktop breakpoints without changing combat math.

L1.recipe: Make useCompactDesktop explicit in every hudFlags() result and restore the legacy desktop branch for standard/tactical density.

L2.recipe: Add missing ability, objective, contract, and performance signals to MobileHUD with accessible labels and focused component tests.

L3.recipe: Build a pure urgency-ranked responsive HUD model, preserve all core capabilities across mobile/compact/tactical modes, add collision-safe disclosure behavior, and enforce parity with architecture and rendering tests.

Generate companion pages, sitemap.xml, footer-manifest.json, agents.json resource routes, and llms route indexes from it. Make validate-public-contract compare actual HTML header/footer links, sitemap URLs, manifests, gameplay-derived roster/mode/weapon facts, and visual-audit coverage against the registry so a stale surface fails closed.

items.title: Make the 22-character art pass an integer-safe, byte-budgeted runtime pipeline instead of loading 4.63 MB of PNGs through fractional atlas rectangles.
items.why: The three 1254x1254 RGBA runtime atlases total 4,634,459 bytes. The four-column atlases yield 313.5px-wide cells, while getRuntimeEnemySprite() divides natural dimensions directly and has no integer coverage invariant, byte ceiling, decode-format choice, or fallback receipt. The art can therefore add first-encounter jank or edge bleed without a failing gate.
items.recipe: Add a deterministic Sharp-backed export step from proprietary source PNGs to compressed WebP runtime atlases, preserve PNG sources, calculate integer cell boundaries with cumulative rounding so every source pixel belongs to exactly one cell, and expose format/fallback metadata. Extend the visual asset manifest validator with per-atlas dimensions, alpha, grid coverage, total runtime-byte ceiling, and required type-index coverage. Preload only the current/next roster atlas and keep the procedural body as truthful fallback.

L1.recipe: Round atlas rectangle boundaries cumulatively and test exact full-image coverage.

L2.recipe: Generate WebP runtime atlases, update consumers, and enforce an aggregate byte ceiling with PNG source preservation.

L3.recipe: Ship deterministic integer-safe export, modern-format delivery, type/grid/alpha/byte validation, bounded preloading, fallback receipts, and regression tests.
